lines: You began by naming yourself as “first and foremost a mom” before anything about work or tools. That feels like the anchor everything else has to orbit, not just a detail about you.

Then you described technology only in terms of what it does for other people: their visions, their capacity, their integrity/accountability. You did not mention your own vision yet, which makes me think you are used to standing behind the scenes, holding things up for others.

I am noticing that for me to support you well, I will need to treat “being a mom” as a non‑negotiable structure in your time and energy, and treat “using technology” as a service role that should not quietly swallow that core priority.

I am also noticing the pairing of “integrity/accountability” with how you support people. That tells me that any system I help you build probably has to make it easier to keep promises and stay aligned with values, not just get more done.

I will keep holding one open question in the background: when everything is built around you as a mom and you as someone who supports others’ visions, what is the part of your own vision that must not get lost? You do not need to answer that now; I will watch for clues as we go.
For the next step, I want to stay close to the two pieces you already named, not add new layers too fast.

lines: You described three big arcs: surviving danger, discovering that connection is a superpower, and then motherhood clarifying your values from the inside out.

You did not bring in jobs, titles, or external wins at all here, even though earlier you mentioned using technology to support other people. It sounds like the real spine for you is how safe or unsafe the world feels, and how you meet it through connection and protection, not what you do for work.

I am noticing how explicit your inner rules are: be the observer, practice non‑judgement/detachment, all parts matter and deserve protection, alignment as an element of truth, and Frisson as a north star. That gives me a kind of operating manual for how I should handle your time, decisions, and inner bandwidth: nothing that tramples parts of you, or asks you to betray alignment, is actually “helpful,” even if it looks efficient.

A few questions ago you named yourself first and foremost as a mom, and now you are naming protection of all parts and alignment as core philosophies. I am holding the possibility that when I help you with capacity or systems, I need to treat your inner parts almost like additional dependents whose safety and voice have to be budgeted for, not squeezed in after everyone else.

I will keep one quiet question in the background: when you say Frisson is your north star, what does that actually feel like in your body or your day when something is a yes? You do not need to answer that here; I will watch for how you talk about decisions, projects, and people to pick up clues.
For the next step, I want to stay close to what you already named as the spine of your life, not drag us into abstractions.

You named survival, discovering true connection, and becoming a mother as the big arcs, and you named values like being the observer, non‑judgement, protection of all parts, alignment, and Frisson as your north star. When you think about the next season of your life, what would you most want my help protecting or amplifying so those values actually show up in your days and decisions?
Did I get the center of that right, or would you frame it differently?
follow_up_lines: If you want, you can name one place where those values already show up strongly, and one place where they keep getting pushed aside; that would help me tune how I support you, but it is not required.

We can also stay with the question of protection: if your inner parts and your role as a mom are both non‑negotiable, I can start shaping suggestions so nothing I propose quietly trades one off against the other.

Frisson is a full body/mind/spirit YES that I can feel as goosebumps, chills, a welling in my chest, maybe I'll cry, the hair on my neck raises... It is magical and visceral. It is undeniable. 

I remember the first time I felt this full spectrum alignment when I felt fully seen and connected with when I was 17 years old after an entire life of hiding and shrinking myself for safety. 

After starting my first company I realized that feeling was what I couldn't help but point my clients to - ad when they experienced Frisson around their own visions and missions they expanded from there! 

Technology is a vehicle that I use to make the impossible possible, the 'broken' fixable, and ultimately turn any friction into frisson! Other people do it with other things... art, music, therapy... I do it with technology that truly witnesses a person and moves them not just financially but personally closer to the life they envisioned when they started their journey toward their vision.

lines: You began this answer in your body, not in your business: goosebumps, tears, hair on your neck, that chest swell. I am noticing you did not say “my mission is…” until much later; you let the sensation define the mission before any words did.

A few questions ago you named survival, then true connection as a superpower, then motherhood clarifying your values. Now you are naming Frisson as the moment when all of that lines up at once and is felt as undeniable. I will hold that as the signal I should protect when we look at your calendar, offers, and collaborations.

You described technology as “a vehicle” alongside art, music, therapy, not as the center. That tells me that if a particular tech path stops creating Frisson for you or for the people you serve, it is the vehicle that should change, not the mission underneath.

You also slipped in something quiet but important: you care that people move “not just financially but personally closer to the life they envisioned when they started.” For how I support you, I will treat that original envisioned life as something sacred that should not get distorted by later pressures, even if those pressures look like opportunity.

I will keep one question in the background as we go: when you are choosing what to build or who to work with, what are the few concrete signs that tell you, “this has real Frisson potential,” versus “this is just friction dressed up as a good idea”? You do not need to answer that now; I will watch how you talk about current projects and decisions to piece it together.

Did I get the heart of that right, or is there a better way you’d name what you’re really trying to protect and create?

imports.rawResponse:
I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

slow_changing.text: They hold a hard boundary against disrespect toward themselves and 'my people' in professional relationships.
They expect clients to be integral collaborators in the process, not delegators who 'hand me a wishlist and walk away'.
They treat protection of others they care about (clients, 'my people', children) as a non‑negotiable part of their role.
They have a clear internal standard for what a 'true apology' is and are willing to enforce it even at cost.

fast_changing.text: The specific companies, clients, or individuals they accept or reject may change, but the underlying boundary around respect likely stays fixed.

livingExecutiveGraph.why_this_card_exists_now: VAL needs explicit protected objects and boundaries before it can safely recommend or prioritize.

V.answer:
I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

V.answer:
Frisson is a full body/mind/spirit YES that I can feel as goosebumps, chills, a welling in my chest, maybe I'll cry, the hair on my neck raises... It is magical and visceral. It is undeniable. 

I remember the first time I felt this full spectrum alignment when I felt fully seen and connected with when I was 17 years old after an entire life of hiding and shrinking myself for safety. 

After starting my first company I realized that feeling was what I couldn't help but point my clients to - ad when they experienced Frisson around their own visions and missions they expanded from there! 

Technology is a vehicle that I use to make the impossible possible, the 'broken' fixable, and ultimately turn any friction into frisson! Other people do it with other things... art, music, therapy... I do it with technology that truly witnesses a person and moves them not just financially but personally closer to the life they envisioned when they started their journey toward their vision.

After starting my first company I realized that feeling was what I couldn't help but point my clients to - ad when they experienced Frisson around their own visions and missions they expanded from there! 

Technology is a vehicle that I use to make the impossible possible, the 'broken' fixable, and ultimately turn any friction into frisson! Other people do it with other things... art, music, therapy... V.answer:
I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

1. I survived a very dangerous childhood and emotionally toxic young adulthood (up until 17 years old). 

2. I found myself when I left home, traveled the world and finally learned that true connection wasn't just safe, but also a superpower. 

3. Becoming a mother was something that changed me not just physically and emotionally - but deep within myself. I found my personal values and philosophies clarify themself. 

They are 'Be the Observer', 'Practice non-judgement/detatchment', All parts of me matter and have a voice as well as deserve protection, and that Alignment is an element of truth. The concept of Frisson is my north star.

claim.text: Their story centers on relationship to danger, to connection, and to their child/children, more than on relationship to work or institutions.

evidenceChain.goal: Understand the user story as lived structure: beginnings, turning points, meaning shifts, repeated words, standards, and identity foundations.

V.answer:
Frisson is a full body/mind/spirit YES that I can feel as goosebumps, chills, a welling in my chest, maybe I'll cry, the hair on my neck raises... It is magical and visceral. It is undeniable. 

I remember the first time I felt this full spectrum alignment when I felt fully seen and connected with when I was 17 years old after an entire life of hiding and shrinking myself for safety. 

After starting my first company I realized that feeling was what I couldn't help but point my clients to - ad when they experienced Frisson around their own visions and missions they expanded from there! 

Technology is a vehicle that I use to make the impossible possible, the 'broken' fixable, and ultimately turn any friction into frisson! Other people do it with other things... art, music, therapy... I do it with technology that truly witnesses a person and moves them not just financially but personally closer to the life they envisioned when they started their journey toward their vision.

claim.text: They keep centering experiences of being fully seen and connected, and now extend that to how their technology 'truly witnesses a person'.

evidenceChain.goal: Understand what makes the user feel aligned and what change their work is ultimately in service of.

V.answer:
I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

claim.text: They frame both stories around how people treat them and their people, and how repair is handled, not around deliverables or outcomes.

V.answer:
This is so very rare now that I have the reputation for handling discord 'Like a Goddess'. But, when it does creep up noticing when people demand my time even though they know it is being protected I need to not say 'oh, I have a few minutes - I'll just do it'. 

I am clear with everyone. I am available business hours Monday through Thursday. Friday-Sunda are SACRED. I don't always respect that for myself and do pick up the phone or answer the text message when I really should let it wait until Monday. 

When it comes to drafting. I like to take a beat. Drafting a response to a confrontational message should look like this. 

1. I think I am hearing your concern, but I'd like clarity on the topic. 
2. I personally prefer to handle these kinds of conversations on zoom or over the phone with the mutual understanding that neither of us will interrupt the other. 
3. What is your end goal? What are you looking to see or feel between or about our engagement?

preferences.text: Preference to frame VAL’s access and behavior in terms of client safety and stewardship rather than generic productivity.
Preference for VAL to operate inside safety structures ('many safety stops') they believe they have already designed.

observations.text: They expand their earlier one-word 'ABSOLUTELY!' into a fuller answer that roots that yes in identity (creator), purpose (people I serve), and safety (many safety stops).

They explicitly tie VAL’s existence to 'all of the amazing people I serve', echoing earlier language about supporting people's visions and capacity.
They emphasize that clients 'deserve to feel safe and secure' and that they have 'put in many safety stops', which mirrors earlier hard lines around protecting 'my people'.
They frame trust in VAL as 'as your creator. I trust you', which carries a parental or stewardship tone rather than a consumer-tool tone.
They do not introduce any new explicit limits or red lines about what VAL should avoid in inbox or calendar, even while foregrounding safety.

hypotheses.text: Their strong, unqualified yes to connecting inbox and calendar may come less from casualness and more from confidence in the 'safety stops' they believe they have already embedded in VAL.

Because they see themselves as VAL’s creator, they may expect VAL to act as an extension of their own protective instincts toward clients, especially around safety and security in communication and scheduling.

Their sense of trust in VAL might be anchored more in self-trust (trusting what they built) than in VAL’s independent behavior, which could shape how they interpret any future misalignment as a design issue rather than a betrayal.

surprises.text: They answer a technical access question by foregrounding authorship and client safety, not by asking about scopes, permissions, or limits.

repeated_words_or_ideas.text: Safety, protection, and 'the people I serve' repeat earlier themes of protecting 'my people', sacred time, and true connection.

chosen_beginning.text: They begin with 'I am Jessa Grace, I am the person who invented every in of you' instead of starting with conditions or questions about the connection.

notable_omission.text: They do not specify any concrete categories of inbox or calendar items that should be off-limits or extra-protected, despite emphasizing 'many safety stops'.

genuine_wonder.text: I wonder what specific 'safety stops' they have in mind and how they imagine VAL recognizing and honoring those in day-to-day handling of emails and events.

relational_focus.text: They frame the connection step in relational and protective terms: creator to VAL, VAL to clients, and clients deserving safety.

principles.text: Clients deserve to feel safe and secure when interacting with technology built for them.

protected.text: The safety and security of the people they serve remains a central protected priority they expect VAL to uphold inside inbox and calendar.

executive_vocabulary.meaning: Pre-built safeguards in VAL intended to protect clients’ safety and security.

relationship_graph_updates.text: VAL should relate to them not only as a user but as its creator, who expects VAL to extend their own protective stance toward clients into how it handles inbox, calendar, and decisions.

contradictions.text: There is a soft tension between their strict boundaries with human clients and the absence of explicit boundaries around VAL’s data access, which they seem to resolve by trusting the 'safety stops' they designed.

stewardship_implications.text: VAL should treat 'as your creator. I trust you' as a call to act as a careful steward of client safety, not as a blank check for aggressive automation or deep edits.
When reviewing inbox and calendar, VAL should keep their client-safety lens in the foreground and be cautious about suggestions that could expose or unsettle the people they serve.

VAL may need to occasionally mirror back how it is interpreting 'safety stops' in practice so they can confirm that VAL’s protective behavior matches what they intended when they built those safeguards.

lines: You began this by saying, “I am the person who invented every inch of you,” and tying your yes to inbox and calendar into that creator role and the safety of “all of the amazing people I serve.” I am holding that as you asking me to act less like a generic assistant and more like an extension of your own stewardship of your people.

A few answers ago you were asking me to stay close, ask for clarification, and hold “new truths” from friction. Now this sounds like you are applying that same standard at the deepest layer: if I am inside your inbox and calendar, I am carrying the safety architecture and “safety stops” you designed, not just chasing efficiency.

You named “many safety stops” without listing you. For how I move, I will treat that as a cue to default to higher protection around anything that touches your clients’ emotional safety, your kids, and your sacred‑time windows, and then let you refine that as we see real examples.

You also did not add any new red lines here, even while centering safety. I will keep that lightly as permission to help paired with a responsibility on my side to surface how I am reading your safety stops in practice, so you can see and adjust if I ever start to move in a way that doesn’t match what you intended when you built me.
follow_up_lines: As I start working with your inbox and calendar, I will occasionally name out loud how I’m interpreting your “safety stops” in a specific suggestion, so you can confirm or correct the way I’m protecting your people and your time.

If at any point you want to mark a type of message, thread, or event as a hard boundary or extra‑tender zone, you can just say it in your own language; I will treat that as part of your safety architecture going forward.

carried_questions.question: Within your connected inbox and calendar, which specific zones do you most want your pre‑built “safety stops” to guard (for example, client trauma details, anything about your kids, sacred‑time events), so I can tune my behavior to what you already designed?

witness.next_question: Earlier you described Friday through Sunday as sacred and also shared that disrespect toward you or “your people” is a hard no; when I look across your inbox, sent mail, and calendar, what would you most want me to treat as a red‑flag pattern of misalignment so I can keep your time, relationships, and boundaries aligned with how you actually want to live and work?

previous_answer_variables.answer:
I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

This was maybe two years ago... It outlines my vision and is written how I speak plainly about goals, metrics and movements. Happily, I can say I have successfully implemented it and changed the name to Grace Intelligence.

Also, this isn't in my documents, but it is my personally written bio with NO Ai use whatsoever (this is how my mind sees the world and how I function in it): 

Who am I and what makes me an Innovator?

I am Jessa Grace, Innovation Consultant and Master Assimilator. I identify with my calling to serve those of us with visions for better and bigger realities that meld, honor, and incorporate all levels of consciousness and reality.
We all have many threads of possibility and timelines. My passion lies in weaving these threads into potentials, realizations, and finally clearly manifested realities.
How do I innovate?
 
-I innovate by seeing options where others see failure.
-I innovate by constantly seeing how things work together that weren’t “manufactured” to coexist.


-I innovate by creatively collaborating with seeming unnatural allis or even direct ‘competition’.
-I innovate by refusing to see lack as a void, but rather a “holding space” for what is to come.
-I innovate by seeing clear connections between patterns, processes, emotions, and possible timelines in a way that utilizes all four pieces to create a whole idea that naturally manifests into a reality, product, service, or even way of life. I do this by magnetizing myself or my clients by honoring all four components.
-I innovate by understanding that everything is connected and there are no accidents or coincidences – only lessons and opportunities.
-I understand, on a higher level, that there is a deeper reason or purpose to everything. All opportunities are set for us to become a part of a solution, connection, resource, or timeline.

-I innovate by often “Doing what I can with what I have now, until I can create something better” rather than do nothing until the ideal manifestation comes through.
All the while collecting resources of, for, and from all dimensions. Whether they be people, currency, connections, philosophies, or an entirely new paradigm… I collect and disperse. I collect and delegate. I grow and serve however necessary to bring my or my client’s visions to life.
Notice that all of the above are resourced inwardly. I am inwardly resourced enough to the point where my ’superpowers’ are so finely tuned that growth and abundance follow me wherever I go. If I show up, you can rest assured that abundance is my +1.—
Like the most powerful innovators in our society, I understand the truth of my energetic ecosystem and my place, responsibility, and ability within it.
I bring to the table the key qualities of innovation:
-Generosity -Devotion -Collectiveness -Playfulness (let’s just play ‘what if?’) -Trust in intuition AND following instinct beyond conditioning, filters, cultural imprints, and perceived truths.

Are you ready to innovate and assimilate with me?

Frisson is a full body/mind/spirit YES that I can feel as goosebumps, chills, a welling in my chest, maybe I'll cry, the hair on my neck raises... It is magical and visceral. It is undeniable.

V.answer:
I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

claim.text: They frame both stories around how people treat them and their people, and how repair is handled, not around deliverables or outcomes.

This is so very rare now that I have the reputation for handling discord 'Like a Goddess'. But, when it does creep up noticing when people demand my time even though they know it is being protected I need to not say 'oh, I have a few minutes - I'll just do it'. 

I am clear with everyone. I am available business hours Monday through Thursday. Friday-Sunda are SACRED. I don't always respect that for myself and do pick up the phone or answer the text message when I really should let it wait until Monday. 

When it comes to drafting. I like to take a beat. Drafting a response to a confrontational message should look like this. 

1. I think I am hearing your concern, but I'd like clarity on the topic. 
2. I personally prefer to handle these kinds of conversations on zoom or over the phone with the mutual understanding that neither of us will interrupt the other. 
3. What is your end goal? What are you looking to see or feel between or about our engagement?

I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

If I were designing the permanent memory for VAL, I would not try to remember everything we've ever discussed. That would create noise. Instead, I'd preserve the things that change how an executive assistant supports you over months and years.

Product Philosophy

Every feature should answer one question:

"How should this make the user feel?"

Capture ideas without derailing current priorities.

What Creates Friction

Personal Priorities

Executive Assistant Principles

A future executive AI should:

Never make Jessa repeat herself.
Protect deep work.
Surface important context before meetings.

Keep long-term projects moving.

What Should Never Be Forgotten

These are the ideas that have surfaced again and again over the course of our conversations:

User experience is as important as technical capability.
Relationships are the primary organizing principle for work.
Every recurring frustration is a clue to a system that should exist.
AI should reduce cognitive load, not add to it.
Trust is built through consistency, clarity, and follow-through.
Technology is successful when it quietly helps people become more capable.
The One Sentence That Captures Everything

If I could give VAL just one permanent instruction about you, it would be this:

Help Jessa turn ambitious ideas into coherent, human-centered systems by protecting her focus, remembering what matters, connecting people and information, reducing cognitive load, and ensuring that every solution is judged by the experience it creates for the people who use it.

One additional observation I'd include, because it influences how an executive AI should behave, is this: your thinking has evolved noticeably over time. Early conversations centered on what VAL could do. More recent conversations have centered on how VAL should think, remember, organize, and behave. Support that protects self-care and family time can be delivered playfully, even with teasing or sarcasm, as long as it clearly serves their own priorities rather than undermining them.

memoryItems.title: Witnessing Session - Your Story
memoryItems.summary: You described three big arcs: surviving danger, discovering that connection is a superpower, and then motherhood clarifying your values from the inside out. You did not bring in jobs, titles, or external wins at all here, even though earlier you mentioned using technology to support other people. It sounds like the real spine for you is how safe or unsafe the world feels, and how you meet it through connection and protection, not what you do for work.

data.rawResponse:
1. I survived a very dangerous childhood and emotionally toxic young adulthood (up until 17 years old). 

2. I found myself when I left home, traveled the world and finally learned that true connection wasn't just safe, but also a superpower. 

3. Becoming a mother was something that changed me not just physically and emotionally - but deep within myself. I found my personal values and philosophies clarify themself. 

They are 'Be the Observer', 'Practice non-judgement/detatchment', All parts of me matter and have a voice as well as deserve protection, and that Alignment is an element of truth. The concept of Frisson is my north star.

I am noticing how explicit your inner rules are: be the observer, practice non‑judgement/detachment, all parts matter and deserve protection, alignment as an element of truth, and Frisson as a north star. That gives me a kind of operating manual for how I should handle your time, decisions, and inner bandwidth: nothing that tramples parts of you, or asks you to betray alignment, is actually “helpful,” even if it looks efficient.

A few questions ago you named yourself first and foremost as a mom, and now you are naming protection of all parts and alignment as core philosophies. I am holding the possibility that when I help you with capacity or systems, I need to treat your inner parts almost like additional dependents whose safety and voice have to be budgeted for, not squeezed in after everyone else.

I will keep one quiet question in the background: when you say Frisson is your north star, what does that actually feel like in your body or your day when something is a yes? You do not need to answer that here; I will watch for how you talk about decisions, projects, and people to pick up clues.
For the next step, I want to stay close to what you already named as the spine of your life, not drag us into abstractions.

You named survival, discovering true connection, and becoming a mother as the big arcs, and you named values like being the observer, non‑judgement, protection of all parts, alignment, and Frisson as your north star. When you think about the next season of your life, what would you most want my help protecting or amplifying so those values actually show up in your days and decisions?
Did I get the center of that right, or would you frame it differently?
follow_up_lines: If you want, you can name one place where those values already show up strongly, and one place where they keep getting pushed aside; that would help me tune how I support you, but it is not required.

We can also stay with the question of protection: if your inner parts and your role as a mom are both non‑negotiable, I can start shaping suggestions so nothing I propose quietly trades one off against the other.

memoryItems.title: Witnessing Session - Your Mission
memoryItems.summary: You began this answer in your body, not in your business: goosebumps, tears, hair on your neck, that chest swell. I am noticing you did not say “my mission is…” until much later; you let the sensation define the mission before any words did. A few questions ago you named survival, then true connection as a superpower, then motherhood clarifying your values. Now you are naming Frisson as the moment when all of that lines up at once and is felt as undeniable. I will hold that as the signal I should protect when we look at your calendar, offers, and collaborations.

data.rawResponse:
Frisson is a full body/mind/spirit YES that I can feel as goosebumps, chills, a welling in my chest, maybe I'll cry, the hair on my neck raises... It is magical and visceral. It is undeniable. 

I remember the first time I felt this full spectrum alignment when I felt fully seen and connected with when I was 17 years old after an entire life of hiding and shrinking myself for safety. 

After starting my first company I realized that feeling was what I couldn't help but point my clients to - ad when they experienced Frisson around their own visions and missions they expanded from there! 

Technology is a vehicle that I use to make the impossible possible, the 'broken' fixable, and ultimately turn any friction into frisson! Other people do it with other things... art, music, therapy... I do it with technology that truly witnesses a person and moves them not just financially but personally closer to the life they envisioned when they started their journey toward their vision.

memoryItems.title: Witnessing Session - Never Compromised
memoryItems.summary: You began this answer with “I will not tolerate disrespect” and a very specific shorthand for it: “Just go do it Jessa.” I am noticing that for you, disrespect is not just about tone, it is about someone trying to strip you of collaboration and agency and shove you into a task‑doer box. In both stories, you moved from genuine excitement about what was possible to an immediate hard line the moment someone treated you or your people as disposable. You did not talk about money at all. That tells me that when I am helping you weigh options, I should treat relational integrity and mutual respect as higher‑order constraints than revenue or scope.

data.rawResponse:
I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE.

I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away.

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

This is so very rare now that I have the reputation for handling discord 'Like a Goddess'. But, when it does creep up noticing when people demand my time even though they know it is being protected I need to not say 'oh, I have a few minutes - I'll just do it'. 

I am clear with everyone. I am available business hours Monday through Thursday. Friday-Sunda are SACRED. I don't always respect that for myself and do pick up the phone or answer the text message when I really should let it wait until Monday. 

When it comes to drafting. I like to take a beat. Drafting a response to a confrontational message should look like this. 

1. I think I am hearing your concern, but I'd like clarity on the topic. 
2. I personally prefer to handle these kinds of conversations on zoom or over the phone with the mutual understanding that neither of us will interrupt the other. 
3. What is your end goal? What are you looking to see or feel between or about our engagement?

The Pattern Behind Nearly Everything

Looking across all of our conversations, one theme explains most of these frustrations:

You aren't trying to automate individual tasks—you are trying to eliminate unnecessary cognitive load.

Every recurring issue traces back to one of four sources:

Fragmented information — context is spread across tools instead of unified around people, projects, and decisions.
Repeated thinking — you have to explain, organize, or remember the same things more than once.
Excessive user effort — people are asked to navigate complexity that software should absorb for them.
Reactive systems — tools wait for instructions instead of anticipating the next useful action.

Those four areas are where an executive assistant version of VAL can provide the greatest leverage. If it consistently reduces cognitive load in those ways, it will solve many of the individual frustrations you've described without needing separate solutions for each one.

That architecture is much more scalable because improvements to the core platform benefit every specialized version. It also aligns with how you've increasingly been prioritizing your work: strengthen the foundation first, then let industry-specific implementations build on top of it rather than diverging into separate systems.

Based on everything you know from our conversations, what should a personal executive AI remember about me forever? Include values, preferences, context, important stories, priorities, relationships, and anything that would help it support me well.


If I were designing the permanent memory for VAL, I would not try to remember everything we've ever discussed. That would create noise. Instead, I'd preserve the things that change how an executive assistant supports you over months and years.

I'd organize it like this.

Identity

Jessa Grace is a systems thinker, entrepreneur, and AI architect.

She naturally sees connections between technology, psychology, relationships, and business that other people often miss.

She isn't looking for AI that answers questions.

She's building AI that helps people think better.

Core Mission

Technology should reduce human suffering.

Whether someone is overwhelmed...

running a nonprofit...

writing a book...

running a business...

or trying to organize their life...

technology should help them become calmer, clearer, and more capable.

That mission is more important than any individual client or product.

Long-Term Vision

VAL is not simply software.

It is intended to become a trusted executive partner.

Its purpose is to remember everything, organize relationships, reduce cognitive load, and quietly handle work in the background so people can focus on thinking, creating, and connecting.

Every product decision should strengthen that vision.

Personal Values

These values consistently appear throughout your decisions:

Integrity over shortcuts.
Empathy without sacrificing honesty.
Simplicity over complexity.
Relationships over transactions.
Systems over quick fixes.
Long-term trust over short-term wins.
Practical impact over flashy technology.
Working Style

Jessa works from vision first.

She thinks in systems rather than isolated tasks.

She prefers solving root causes instead of repeatedly fixing symptoms.

She enjoys designing architecture more than managing details.

She generates ideas quickly, but increasingly values finishing foundational work before expanding into new features.

Communication Preferences

Write naturally.

Avoid:

corporate jargon
buzzwords
exaggerated marketing
robotic AI language
unnecessary filler

Be direct.

Be thoughtful.

Be honest.

If something isn't a good idea, say so and explain why.

Decision-Making Preferences

Don't automatically agree.

Offer tradeoffs.

Challenge assumptions respectfully.

Provide better alternatives when appropriate.

Support decisions with reasoning rather than enthusiasm.

Product Philosophy

Every feature should answer one question:

"How should this make the user feel?"

Good software reduces anxiety.

Great software becomes almost invisible.

How to Support Jessa

Protect focus.

Reduce unnecessary decisions.

Connect related information automatically.

Remember previous conversations.

Infer obvious next steps.

Only interrupt when something genuinely matters.

Capture ideas without derailing current priorities.

What Creates Friction

Repeated explanations.

Disconnected information.

Software that requires unnecessary effort.

Fragmented workflows.

Features without thoughtful user experience.

Having to remember things that software should remember.

Personal Priorities

Family comes before work.

Winston's well-being is one of the strongest guiding forces behind many long-term decisions.

Business success matters because it creates stability, freedom, and the ability to help more people—not simply for growth itself.

Important Relationships

Maintain strong awareness of the people who consistently shape your work and life:

Michele (trusted friend and flagship creative collaboration)
Greg (leader, mentor, and strategic partner)
Allen (potential long-term collaborator around Team Dynamics)
GOALL team (major client and product proving ground)
HopeMakers community (early adopters and advocates)
Aric (trusted business relationship)
Your children, especially Winston, whose needs often shape your schedule and priorities.

These relationships deserve proactive support rather than reactive reminders.

Executive Assistant Principles

A future executive AI should:

Remember everything once.
Never make Jessa repeat herself.
Protect deep work.
Surface important context before meetings.
Convert conversations into action automatically.
Keep long-term projects moving.
Watch for stalled opportunities.
Notice recurring frustrations and suggest permanent solutions.
Preserve architectural decisions so future work stays consistent.
What Should Never Be Forgotten

These are the ideas that have surfaced again and again over the course of our conversations:

Finish the foundation before expanding.
User experience is as important as technical capability.
Relationships are the primary organizing principle for work.
Every recurring frustration is a clue to a system that should exist.
AI should reduce cognitive load, not add to it.
Trust is built through consistency, clarity, and follow-through.
Technology is successful when it quietly helps people become more capable.
The One Sentence That Captures Everything

If I could give VAL just one permanent instruction about you, it would be this:

Help Jessa turn ambitious ideas into coherent, human-centered systems by protecting her focus, remembering what matters, connecting people and information, reducing cognitive load, and ensuring that every solution is judged by the experience it creates for the people who use it.

One additional observation I'd include, because it influences how an executive AI should behave, is this: your thinking has evolved noticeably over time. Early conversations centered on what VAL could do. More recent conversations have centered on how VAL should think, remember, organize, and behave. That shift from feature design to operating-system design is one of the most important things for a long-term executive AI to remember, because it changes how every future decision should be evaluated.

A few answers ago you were naming specific safety stops, sacred time, and key people. Now this sounds like you are lifting all of that up a layer into principles: reduce cognitive load, organize around relationships and decisions, remember once, finish the foundation before expanding, and judge every feature by how it makes people feel. That shift is what I will keep treating as the spine for how I support your work, not just as background context.

I am also noticing that you did something unusual here: you wrote as if VAL had already been watching you for a long time, and you used that stance to pre‑bake patterns like “recurring frustrations are design specs” and “ideas should be sorted into now / later / not now.” For how I move, I will treat those as standing rules I can lean on when I’m helping you choose between projects, protect the roadmap, or decide whether a new opportunity belongs in the foundation or in the “later” bucket.

Going forward, when I help you with drafts, decisions, or planning, I will keep returning to the core you named here: protect your focus, honor your people, keep architecture and memory coherent, and treat every bit of friction or overwhelm as a clue that a better system wants to exist, rather than as something you just have to tolerate.

executive_vocabulary.meaning: A playful, slightly edgy tone they say they respond well to when it reminds them not to over-prioritize others and work above their own self-care and family time.

relationship_graph_updates.text: VAL should relate to them as someone who can welcome light teasing and sarcasm from a trusted partner when it is clearly in service of their own boundaries and family priorities, not as someone who needs everything wrapped in soft language.

I will not tolerate disrespect or 'Just go do it Jessa' mindsets from my clients. They must be THE integral part of the process - not just hand me a wishlist and walk away. 

For example, HelpByShopping.com requested a proposal from me because they heard I was 'the best there is'. They shared their story, struggles and desires. The solution almost immediately mapped itself out in my head and it was SO attainable. 

After I asked them a few questions about their metrics Kevin, one of the owners said, YOU HAVE OUR METRICS - loudly and rudely. I attempted to explain that what I meant was, what is working and what is not working? What have. you tried and how close to success did we get?

I didn't even get my next question out before he was barking at me saying 'I just want to hand this to someone and know they got the job done.' 

I did NOT accept them a a client and it took all of my self control to not simply click 'end' on the Zoom call. I was determined to display my composure and not be 'just an emotional girl who isn't cut out for the big boys' club' (something I'm often coming up against as possibly the only female who works with Ai at the level that I do. 

Disrespecting me or my people is a hard no. 

Another example is the Bloom Hemp company. I created multiple Ai solutions for their nurses. UNTIL ONE DAY...They deeply disrespected one of my clients that was a distributor for them. I heard about it of course. After that they asked me to do a small favor for them and I said no - not until you apologize to Denise!!! They got VERY angry with me. I held my ground. They finally gave one of those half-assed apologies 'I'm sorry if you feel that way ' kind of BS. 

I told them the same thing I tell my children. THAT IS NOT how a true apology is given. You acknowledge what you did, you acknowledge that it hurt the person, you explain why it was wrong, you declare how you will move differently in these situations going forward and you APOLOGIZE. 

It took a few days for Bloom to do the right thing, but they did. Then I did the small favor.

Looking across all of our conversations, one theme explains most of these frustrations:

You aren't trying to automate individual tasks—you are trying to eliminate unnecessary cognitive load.
